analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch hunk at head lines 2492-2512 adds prose about Flint constrained-decode chaining, the automatic paged list for RecursiveSI/flint-int4, and fused decode kernels. Both supplied units (head lines 1209-2032) cover unchanged surrounding documentation; the changed range lies outside them, so I could not see the added text in the numbered units and relied on the patch excerpt.

Security relevance: no code, config defaults, trust boundaries or mitigations change. The documentation states the constrained-chaining token stream is identical to unchained decode, and that the mask cache is keyed by constraint state. Cached masks are derived from public constraint state, not prompt content, so I see no new cross-tenant leakage path. This does not touch T-041's prefix-cache, HMAC lookup, TTL or salt controls.

The doc also says flint-int4 starts at the legacy serving width without an operator override. That describes a non-code behavior claim that cannot be verified from the supplied evidence. Memory admission and the serving-qualification gates are described elsewhere as unchanged. The claims of byte-identical outputs and primitive reduction are unverified documentation assertions. They do not alter the threat model on their own.

Unverified: the actual Swift implementation of chaining (redraw from retained logits, RNG state restoration), the mask cache and the fused kernels is outside this PR's supplied evidence. If the corresponding code lands in the same PR, review it for cross-request state leakage in the cached device masks and the retained logits. No finding is warranted from this documentation-only batch.
